data.name: Muralidhar
data.gender_notes: Muralidhar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Murali (God's abode) + Dhar (holder) – One who holds or preserves the divine abode. The name Muralidhar carries the meaning “God's abode holder” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Muralidhar usually hope their child will grow to embody god's abode holder and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing devotion and dedication to the divine.
data.etymology: Muralidhar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's abode holder.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Muralidhar total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Muralidhar holds great cultural significance in Indian art and literature. It is often associated with Lord Krishna, who is believed to dwell in the hearts of his devotees. The name evokes images of Krishna playing the flute, enchanting the Gopis and filling their hearts with love and devotion. The name is also popular among Hindu scholars, philosophers, and poets.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Muralidhar emphasizes the concept of God as the ultimate refuge and abode of the soul. It invites the devotee to surrender their mind, body, and spirit to the divine, seeking His protection, guidance, and love. The name is a reminder of the eternal and unbreakable bond between the divine and the self, and the importance of holding on to that divine connection with steadfast faith and devotion.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Muralidhar: Beloved of Murari (Krishna). A devotee, eternally immersed in the love of Lord Krishna.

historical_references.reference: Muralidhar was a revered 16th century Hindu saint, philosopher, and poet from the South Indian state of Andhra Pradesh. He is considered an incarnation of Lord Krishna and is known for his devotion to the deity.

Another account suggests that Muralidhar was a renowned scholar and poet in the 13th or 14th century, and is believed to have written several works in Sanskrit and Telugu on Hindu philosophy and literature.
